current_example.problem:
Let $v(t)$ denote the speed (in $\textrm{km/h}$) of a hurricane at time $t$ (in hours) since the hurricane originated in the Atlantic Ocean. The graph of $y=v'(t),$ the derivative of $v(t),$ is given below. Find all the values of $t$ where the speed of the hurricane is decreasing. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193353/assets/9e93a8c0657797100f23b229be1a41c2c377a1711b33b4fc51fc44c8b5b03f89.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following:

- If $v'(t) = 0$ for all $t \in (a,b),$ then $v(t)$ is constant on $(a,b).$

- When $v'(t) > 0$ for all $t \in (a,b),$ then $v(t)$ is increasing on $(a,b).$

- When $v'(t) <             0$ for all $t \in (a,b),$ then $v(t)$ is decreasing on $(a,b).$

From the above graph, we can see that $v'(t)$ is negative on the intervals $[0,2)$ and $(7,8]\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193353/assets/e2f4f59a5ea966ec9927caed5a870c57d63b19654330ced524998787f5837e49.png)

Therefore, the speed of the hurricane is decreasing when $t \in [0,2) \cup (7,8].$
